hypervault/reference/cli/mc-mv.title: mc mv | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-mv.text: mc mv The mc mv command moves an object from source to the target, such as between MinIO AIStor deployments or between buckets on the same MinIO AIStor deployment. mc mv also supports moving objects between a local filesystem and MinIO AIStor. You can also use mc mv against the local filesystem to produce similar results to the mv command-line tool. Syntax Example The following command moves objects from the mydata bucket to the archive bucket on the myaistor MinIO AIStor deployment: mc mv --recursive myaistor/mydata myaistor/archive Syntax The command has the following syntax: mc [GLOBALFLAGS

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-od.title: mc od | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-od.text: mc od The mc od command copies a local file to a remote location in a specified number of parts and part sizes. The command outputs the time it took to upload the file. Use the mc od to mimic the functionality of the Linux dd command. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-qos-rule.text: mc qos rule Description The mc qos rule commands allow you to manage Quality of Service (QoS) rules on a MinIO AIStor deployment. QoS rules enable you to control API request rates and concurrency to ensure fair resource allocation and prevent system overload. Rules can be configured based on API operations, bucket patterns, and object prefixes. For more information, see Bucket-level Quality of Service. Added in RELEASE.2025-12-20T04-58-37Z mc qos rule and its subcommands require AIStor Client RELEASE.2025-12-19T20-11-44Z or later and AIStor Server RELEASE.2025-12-20T04-58-37Z or later. Subcomm

For more information, see Bucket-level Quality of Service. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-quota.title: mc quota | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-quota.text: mc quota The mc quota commands configure, display, or clear a hard quota on a bucket. When a bucket reaches its configured hard quota, MinIO AIStor rejects further write operations until data is removed to bring usage below the limit. See Bucket Quotas for a complete overview of quota behavior and monitoring. This command replaces the deprecated mc admin bucket quota command. Subcommands The mc quota command includes the following subcommands: Subcommand Description set Sets a hard quota on a bucket. info Displays the current quota configuration for a bucket. clear Removes the quota configurat

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-quota/mc-quo.title: mc quota set | HyperVault Documentation

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-rb.title: mc rb | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-rb.text: mc rb The mc rb command removes one or more buckets on MinIO AIStor or another S3-compatible service. To remove only the contents of a bucket, use mc rm instead. mc rb permanently deletes bucket(s) on the target deployment, including any and all object versions and bucket configurations such as lifecycle management or replication. You can also use mc rb against the local filesystem to produce similar results to the rm --rf command-line tool. Syntax Example The following command removes the mydata bucket on the myaistor MinIO AIStor deployment: mc rb --force myaistor/mydata Syntax The command h

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-ready.title: mc ready | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-ready.text: mc ready The mc ready command checks the status of a cluster and whether the cluster has read and write quorum. Example The following sends a GET request to the cluster at alias myaistor and returns its status. mc ready myaistor The command sends a GET request to the deployment at the alias myaistor.’ The command repeats the request until it is successful. The output before the cluster at alias myaistor is ready resembles the following: The cluster `myaistor` is unreachable: Get "http://myaistor.example.com:9000/minio/health/cluster": dial tcp 198.51.100.0:9000: connect: connection refused Onc

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-replicate.title: mc replicate | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-replicate.text: mc replicate The mc replicate command configures and manages per-bucket Server-Side Bucket Replication for a MinIO AIStor deployment, including active-active replication configurations and resynchronization. For site-level replication, see mc admin replicate. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-replicate/mc.title: mc replicate add | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-replicate/mc.text: mc replicate add MinIO AIStor automatically creates remote targets based on a given file path or resource location (such as an IP or DNS address). Users defining a remote target no longer need to determine an ARN for the remote bucket. The mc replicate add command creates a new server-side replication rule for a bucket on a MinIO AIStor deployment. The remote bucket must be on a MinIO AIStor deployment running the same version of MinIO AIStor as the local deployment. Where mc mirror only synchronizes the current version of an object, mc replicate synchronizes all versions, version information,

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-replicate/mc.title: mc replicate backlog | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-replicate/mc.text: mc replicate backlog The mc replicate backlog shows a list of unreplicated new or deleted objects. mc replicate diff is a legacy alias of mc replicate backlog. Both run the same command, so mc replicate diff --help displays this page’s backlog reference. Use mc replicate backlog. You can list the replication status of objects for a particular remote target. To do so, you must have the ARN of the remote target. You can mc replicate ls and mc replicate status to retrieve the remote targets configured for a bucket and find the ARN. Syntax Example The following command exports the replication configuration for the mydata bucket on the myaistor MinIO AIStor deployment: mc replicate export myaistor/mydata > mydata-replication.json Syntax The command has the following syntax: mc [GLOBALFLAGS] export ALIAS Brackets [] indicate optional parameters. Parameters sharing a line are mutually dependent. Parameters separated using the pipe |

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-replicate/mc.title: mc replicate resync | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-replicate/mc.text: mc replicate resync The mc replicate resync command resynchronizes all objects in the specified MinIO AIStor bucket to a remote replication target. This command requires first configuring the remote bucket target using the mc replicate add command. Identify that target with --remote-bucket, which accepts either ALIAS/BUCKET or the destination ARN on AIStor Client RELEASE.2025-07-28T19-02-30Z and later. Earlier versions require the ARN. Use this command when replication is stuck or when you need to manually trigger replication for objects with PENDING or FAILED replication status. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-retention.title: mc retention | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-retention.text: mc retention The mc retention command configures the Write-Once Read-Many (WORM) locking settings for an object or object(s) in a bucket. You can also set the default object lock settings for a bucket, where all objects without explicit object lock settings inherit the bucket default. Subcommands mc retention includes the following subcommands: Subcommand Description clear Clears object retention settings for a bucket or object. info Display the retention settings for a bucket or object. set Set or update the retention settings for a bucket or object.

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-retention/mc.title: mc retention clear | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-retention/mc.text: mc retention clear The mc retention clear command removes the Write-Once Read-Many (WORM) locking settings for an object or object(s) in a bucket. You can also remove the default object lock settings for a bucket. To change the retention status of an object under legal hold, use mc legalhold clear. Syntax Example The following command removes the default object lock configuration for the mydata bucket on the myaistor MinIO AIStor deployment: mc retention clear --default myaistor/mydata Syntax The command has the following syntax: mc [GLOBALFLAGS] retention clear \ [--default] \ [--recursive] \

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-retention/mc.title: mc retention info | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-retention/mc.text: mc retention info The mc retention info command configures the Write-Once Read-Many (WORM) locking settings for an object or object(s) in a bucket. You can also set the default object lock settings for a bucket, where all objects without explicit object lock settings inherit the bucket default. To lock an object under legal hold, use mc legalhold set. mc retention info requires that the specified bucket has object locking enabled. You can enable object locking at bucket creation. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-retention/mc.text: mc retention set The mc retention set command configures the Write-Once Read-Many (WORM) locking settings for an object or object(s) in a bucket. You can also set the default object lock settings for a bucket, where all objects without explicit object lock settings inherit the bucket default. To lock an object under legal hold, use mc legalhold set. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-rm.title: mc rm | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-rm.text: mc rm The mc rm command removes objects from a bucket on a MinIO AIStor deployment. To completely remove a bucket, use mc rb instead. You can also use mc rm against the local filesystem to produce similar results to the rm command-line tool. For more information on how MinIO AIStor performs DELETE actions on objects, see Object Deletion. mc rm supports removing multiple objects or files in a single command. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-share.title: mc share | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-share.text: mc share Use the mc share commands to manage presigned URLs for downloading and uploading objects to a bucket. Subcommands mc share includes the following subcommands: Subcommand Description mc share download The mc share download command creates URLs for performing GET operations mc share list The mc share list command lists active share URLs mc share upload The mc share upload command creates URLs for performing PUT operations

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-share/mc-sha.title: mc share download | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-share/mc-sha.text: mc share download The mc share download command generates a temporary presigned URL with integrated access credentials for downloading objects from a MinIO AIStor bucket. The temporary URL expires after a configurable time limit. Applications can perform a GET to retrieve the object from the URL. Users can open the URL in a browser to download the object. For more information on shareable object URLs, see the Amazon S3 documentation on Pre-Signed URLs. Syntax Example The following command generates a new presigned download URL for the mydata bucket on the myaistor MinIO AIStor deployment: mc s

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-share/mc-sha.title: mc share list | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-share/mc-sha.text: mc share list The mc share ls command displays any unexpired presigned URLs generated by mc share upload or mc share download. The mc share list command has equivalent functionality to mc share ls. Applications use a GET request against a download URL to retrieve an object, or a PUT request against an upload URL to store one. For more information on shareable object URLs, see the Amazon S3 documentation on Pre-Signed URLs. Syntax Example The following commands list all unexpired upload and download presigned URLs respectively: mc share ls upload mc share ls download Syntax The command has the

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-share/mc-sha.title: mc share upload | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-share/mc-sha.text: mc share upload The mc share upload command generates a temporary presigned URL with integrated access credentials for uploading objects to a MinIO AIStor bucket. The temporary URL expires after a configurable time limit. Applications can perform a PUT to upload an object using the URL. Syntax Example The following command generates a new presigned upload URL for the mydata bucket on the myaistor MinIO AIStor deployment: mc share upload --recursive myaistor/mydata Syntax The command has the follo

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-sql.title: mc sql | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-sql.text: mc sql The mc sql command provides an S3 Select interface for performing sql queries on objects in the specified MinIO AIStor deployment. See Selecting content from objects for more information on S3 Select behavior and limitations. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-stat.title: mc stat | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-stat.text: mc stat The mc stat command displays information on objects in a MinIO AIStor bucket, including object metadata. You can also use it to retrieve bucket metadata. You can use mc stat against the local filesystem to produce similar results to the stat command-line tool. Syntax Example The following command displays information on all objects in the mydata bucket on the myaistor MinIO AIStor deployment: mc stat --recursive myaistor/mydata Syntax The command has the following syntax: mc [GLOBALFLAGS] stat \ [--enc-c "value"] \ [--no-list] \ [--recursive] \ [--rewind "string"] \ [--versions] \ [--v

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support.title: mc support | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support.text: mc support The AIStor Client mc support commands provides tools for analyzing deployment health or performance and for running diagnostics. You can also upload generated health reports for further analysis by MinIO AIStor engineering. mc support proxy set and mc support proxy remove are exceptions, as you may need to set up a proxy to complete the deployment registration. Subcommands mc support includes the following subcommands: Subcommand Description callhome mc support callhome allows the enabling or disabling of diagnostic reports from a deployment to MinIO SUBNET. diag mc support diag gen

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.title: mc support callhome | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.text: mc support callhome The mc support callhome command allows the enabling or disabling of sending diagnostic reports from a deployment to SUBNET. With Call Home, MinIO AIStor automatically sends a deployment’s diagnostic information to SUBNET. This makes it easier and quicker for the MinIO AIStor team to respond to questions and issues. MinIO AIStor enables this functionality by default for registered clusters. If you prefer not to automatically send these reports to SUBNET, you may disable callhome. Subcommands mc support callhome enable Begin sending a deployment’s diagnostic information to SU

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.title: mc support diag | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.text: mc support diag The mc support diag command generates a health report for a MinIO AIStor deployment. The command generates and uploads the health report to SUBNET for analysis. Automated with Call Home The report is automatically generated and uploaded every 24 hours with Call Home, which can be disabled or enabled at any time. The resulting health report is intended for use by MinIO Engineering through SUBNET and may contain internal or private data points. Exercise caution before sending a health report to a third party or posting the health report in a public forum. MinIO recommends that yo

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.title: mc support inspect | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.text: mc support inspect The mc support inspect command collects the data and metadata associated to objects at the specified path. If this information is required to diagnose a SUBNET issue, MinIO AIStor Engineering will provide the appropriate command. MinIO AIStor assembles this data from each backend drive storing an erasure shard for each specified object. For registered clusters, the file uploads to MinIO AIStor for use by the engineering team in support efforts. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.title: mc support perf | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.text: mc support perf Use the mc support perf command to review the performance of the S3 API (read/write), network IO, and storage (drive read/write). The resulting tests can provide general guidance of deployment performance under S3 GET and PUT requests and identify any potential bottlenecks. For more complete performance testing, consider using a combination of load-testing using your staging application environments and the MinIO Warp S3 benchmarking tool. Use this command to identify potential drive performance bottlenecks in your deployment. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.title: mc support perf object | HyperVault Documentation

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.title: mc support perf site-replication | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.text: mc support perf site-replication The mc support perf site-replication command measures the speed of site replication operations from the specified ALIAS to other configured peers. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.title: mc support profile | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.text: mc support profile mc support profile runs a system profile for your deployment. The results of the profile can provide insight into the Object Store process running on a given node. The resulting report is intended for use by MinIO AIStor Engineering. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-support/mc-s.text: mc support telemetry proxy The mc support telemetry proxy command streams API events from all nodes on the MinIO AIStor deployment to the specified remote OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP)-compatible collector. MinIO AIStor introduces support for Tables in minio RELEASE.2026-02-02T23-40-11Z and mc version RELEASE.2026-02-03T00-12-26Z. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table-share.text: mc table share The mc table share command manages Table Sharing configurations on MinIO AIStor clusters. Table Sharing allows you to share table data with external consumers using a standard open protocol. Each share configuration describes a group of tables and access control tokens that gate access to the shared data. Update to at least RELEASE.2026-02-19T10-32-25Z to access Delta Sharing features. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table config The mc table config command generates query engine configuration for connecting to an Iceberg catalog on a MinIO AIStor cluster. The generated configuration includes the catalog endpoint, warehouse, and credentials from the mc alias. This simplifies setting up query engines like Trino or Spark to work with AIStor Tables. Example The following command generates Trino connector configuration for the my-warehouse warehouse on the myaistor MinIO AIStor cluster: mc table config myaistor my-warehouse --trino Syntax The command has the following syntax: mc [GLOBALFLAGS] table config \

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table create The mc table create command creates a new Iceberg table on a MinIO AIStor cluster. Tables are created within a namespace and can have custom properties. Example The following command creates a table named sales_data in the prod namespace of the analytics warehouse on the myaistor MinIO AIStor cluster: mc table create myaistor analytics prod sales_data \ --schema '{"type":"struct","fields":[{"id":1,"name":"id","type":"long","required":true}]}' Syntax The command has the following syntax: mc [GLOBALFLAGS] table create \ ALIAS \ WAREHOUSE \ NAMESPACE \ TABLE \ --schema "JSON" \ [-

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table encrypt The mc table encrypt command manages server-side encryption for Iceberg warehouses and tables on MinIO AIStor clusters. Encryption can be set at the warehouse level, where it becomes the default for the objects the warehouse stores, or at the table level to override the warehouse default for a single table. Subcommands mc table encrypt includes the following subcommands: Subcommand Description set Set encryption on a warehouse or table. info Show the encryption configuration. clear Remove encryption from a warehouse. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table encrypt clear The mc table encrypt clear command removes the server-side encryption configuration from an Iceberg warehouse. Warehouse scope only This command operates on warehouses only. Table-level encryption cannot be cleared: there is no command to remove a table-level override and return a table to the warehouse default. Example The following command shows the encryption configuration for the mywarehouse warehouse on the myaistor MinIO AIStor cluster: mc table encrypt info myaistor mywarehouse Syntax The command has the following syntax: mc [GLOBALFLAGS] table encrypt info \ ALIAS \ WAREHOUSE \ [NAMESPACE TABLE] Brackets [] indicate optional parameters

Specify three arguments to set encryption on a warehouse, or five arguments to set encryption on a specific table. Table-level encryption overrides the warehouse default for that table. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table namespace The mc table namespace command manages Iceberg namespaces on MinIO AIStor clusters. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table namespace create The mc table namespace create command creates a new Iceberg namespace within a warehouse on a MinIO AIStor cluster. Example The following command creates a namespace named prod in the analytics warehouse on the myaistor MinIO AIStor cluster: mc table namespace create myaistor analytics prod Syntax The command has the following syntax: mc [GLOBALFLAGS] table namespace create \ ALIAS \ WAREHOUSE \ NAMESPACE \ [--at

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table replicate The mc table replicate command manages table replication for AIStor Tables. Use these subcommands to monitor replication, fail over to the DR site, and recover the old primary after a failover. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.title: mc table replicate backfill start | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table replicate backfill start The mc table replicate backfill start command starts a catalog identity backfill across all warehouses. The backfill scans all warehouses and populates missing catalog identity records for namespaces, tables, and views. Only one backfill can run at a time; if a backfill is already in progress, the command fails. The command returns immediately. The backfill runs asynchronously. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.title: mc table replicate backfill status | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table replicate backfill status The mc table replicate backfill status command shows the status of the most recent catalog identity backfill. The output reports the backfill status, when it started and finished, any error, and result counts for warehouses, namespaces, tables, and views, along with any warnings. If no backfill has been run yet, the command reports that no backfill has been run. Example The following command shows the backfill status on the myaistor MinIO AIStor cluster: mc table replicate backfill status myaistor Syntax The command has the following syntax: mc [GLOBALFLAGS]

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.title: mc table replicate catalog | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table replicate catalog The mc table replicate catalog command manages the replica catalog for AIStor Tables. Use these subcommands to recover a replica catalog that is corrupted or out of sync by rebuilding it from the underlying table data. Subcommands mc table replicate catalog includes the following subcommands: Subcommand Description reset Reset the replica catalog so it is rebuilt from scratch. For the end-to-end failover and recovery workflow, see Site Replication and Disaster Recovery.

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.title: mc table replicate catalog reset | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table replicate catalog reset The mc table replicate catalog reset command resets the replica catalog so the catalog scanner rebuilds it from scratch. The command backs up the replica’s table catalog and then deletes it, so the catalog scanner rebuilds it from the underlying table data on the next scan cycle. Use this when the catalog is corrupted or out of sync and needs to be regenerated. A timestamped backup of the old catalog is created automatically. Restoring from the backup requires manual intervention. The command returns immediately. The backup, delete, and rebuild happen asynchron

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.title: mc table replicate failover | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table replicate failover The mc table replicate failover command starts failover and promotion on a replica site. Run this command against a replica when the primary site becomes unavailable and you want to promote the replica to accept write traffic. The command signals the catalog scanner to complete its current cycle at full speed, after which the site stops behaving as a replica and begins accepting client writes. The command returns immediately. Promotion happens asynchronously when the scan cycle completes. After failover completes, the old primary requires manual intervention before

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.title: mc table replicate resync | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table replicate resync The mc table replicate resync command demotes an old primary back to a replica after a failover. After a failover promotes the DR site, the old primary must be demoted before it can rejoin the replication group. This is a two-phase process: first open a resync window on the old primary, resync object data from the new primary, then rebuild the old primary’s catalog to converge on the new primary. Subcommands mc table replicate resync includes the following subcommands: Subcommand Description open Open the post-failover resync window on the new replica. rebuild Rebuild

hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.title: mc table replicate resync open | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table replicate resync open The mc table replicate resync open command opens the post-failover resync window on the new replica. This is phase one of the post-failover catalog resync. Run it against the site you are demoting to be the new replica, which is the old primary. The command opens a resync window so site replication from the new primary can copy objects onto this site: inbound warehouse-bucket replication is permitted again, while client writes are still rejected as on a replica. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.title: mc table replicate resync rebuild | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table replicate resync rebuild The mc table replicate resync rebuild command rebuilds the new replica’s catalog so it converges on the new primary. This is phase two of the post-failover catalog resync. Run it against the site you are demoting to be the new replica, which is the old primary, after mc table replicate resync open and after the site replication resync from the new primary has completed. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.title: mc table replicate status | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table replicate status The mc table replicate status command shows table replication status for a MinIO AIStor cluster. The output reports the catalog scanner status and, for each warehouse, namespace, table, and view, the verified version, the latest version, how many versions the replica is behind, and any missing files. When a post-failover catalog rebuild is in progress, the output also reports the rebuild state and attempts. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.title: mc table show | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table show The mc table show command displays metadata for an Iceberg table on a MinIO AIStor cluster. mc table info is an alias for this command. The output includes the table schema, properties, the table’s UUID, and other metadata. The metadata output includes the table’s UUID, which is the identifier used in IAM table ARNs of the form arn:aws:s3tables:::bucket/{warehouse}/table/{uuid}. The UUID is stable across renames, so UUID-based policies continue to apply even if the table is renamed. For details on using the UUID in policies, see Controlling access to AIStor Tables. See Tag-based access control for the tag rules and for how to reference tags in policies. To manage tags on warehouses instead of tables, use mc table warehouse tag. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.title: mc table view | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table view The mc table view command manages Iceberg views on MinIO AIStor clusters. Views are virtual tables defined by SQL queries. They provide a way to save and reuse query logic without materializing the results. Views can have multiple SQL representations with different dialects for cross-engine compatibility. hypervault/reference/cli/mc-table/mc-tab.text: mc table warehouse The mc table warehouse command manages Iceberg warehouses on MinIO AIStor clusters. hypervault/reference/kubernetes/environm.text: Environment Variable Configuration You can configure MinIO AIStor behavior by setting environment variables using the ObjectStore custom resource. The Operator writes these variables to a configuration file accessible by all MinIO AIStor Pods in the object store. Overview Version changed Support for valueFrom with configMapKeyRef and secretKeyRef requires Operator version RELEASE.2025-10-16T16-46-38Z or later. hypervault/reference/kubernetes/pvc-prot.title: PVC Protection | HyperVault Documentation
hypervault/reference/kubernetes/pvc-prot.text: PVC Protection This page describes PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) protection for MinIO AIStor deployments on Kubernetes. When enabled, PVC protection prevents accidental data loss by blocking PVC deletion until the protection is explicitly removed. How PVC protection works Kubernetes uses finalizers to prevent the deletion of resources until specific cleanup operations complete. The MinIO AIStor Operator can add the aistor.min.io/pvc-protection finalizer to all PVCs created by an Object Store deployment. hypervault/reference/kubernetes/spread-z.text: Spread Zone Configuration Added in Operator RELEASE.2025-10-16T16-46-38Z Spread zone configuration requires Operator version RELEASE.2025-10-16T16-46-38Z or later. Spread zone configuration ensures that MinIO AIStor distributes Pods across configured zones to optimize availability and resiliency in the event any single worker node fails. Overview The Operator supports spread zone configuration by allowing you to specify zones in the topology of your cluster at the pool level.
